tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.content:
1	# Feature Specification: P-RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `011-settings-dashboard` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-10-24
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "P-RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard: Build the Settings screen with the evolution dashboard, and the profile and account actions that live on it. Requirement and acceptance criteria: docs/input/requirements.md, section 1, RF09; RNF05 (section 4) for account deletion. Prototype states: 'Tela 6 — Configurações' in its four dashboard variations and 'Tela 6 — Confirmar exclusão de conta' (prototype extract, section 2.6); profile name editing, 'Sair' and 'Apagar conta'. Backend: GET /dashboard/aggregate, GET /dashboard/narrative, PATCH /account/settings, DELETE /account, POST /auth/logout. Depends on: F000, RF01. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements, section 2), or change the backend."
10	
11	## Clarifications
12	
13	### Session 2026-10-24
14	
15	- Q: What should the dashboard show for an account with more than one entry but not yet enough to fill the chart's full set of bars (e.g. 5 or 15 entries) — a state the spec's three enumerated scenarios (zero / exactly one / more than thirty) never covered? → A: Render the multi-bar chart using whatever of the ten bars the aggregate's buckets actually populate — naturally partial for a small count — and request the narrative for any count of two or more; "more than thirty" is the seed count chosen to reliably exercise a fully-populated demo chart, not a distinct functional threshold.
16	- Q: For the fixed `all` period, which can span anywhere from a few days to years of history, how should the backend's date-bucketed aggregate be mapped onto the chart's fixed ten bars? → A: Client-side, divide the account's full date range (date of the first entry through today) into ten roughly-equal time slices and sum the backend's per-date counts that fall within each slice to produce each bar's value.
17	- Q: Should the Face ID/Touch ID toggle be hidden entirely or shown-but-disabled on a device with no usable biometric capability? → A: Hidden entirely — the toggle row is omitted from Settings rather than shown in a disabled state.
18	
19	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
20	
21	### User Story 1 - Seeing your evolution dashboard (Priority: P1)
22	
23	The user opens the Settings screen and sees, at a glance, a chart of how their recorded entries have built up over time, plus a short AI-written paragraph that puts that pattern into words. Whether they have no entries yet, just one, or a long history, the screen always shows something coherent rather than breaking or looking empty by accident.
24	
25	**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF09 — without a correctly rendering chart and narrative, the feature does not exist. **Scope: aggregation and rendering only — the quality of the AI-written narrative text is never evaluated.**
26	
27	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening Settings for accounts seeded with zero, one, and more than thirty entries respectively, and confirming each renders its own distinct, non-crashing state with the correct chart and text.
28	
29	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
30	
31	1. **Given** the user has zero entries, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a light-gray placeholder chart icon (no chart) and the text "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui", with no AI narrative paragraph shown or requested.
32	2. **Given** the user has exactly one entry, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a single small bar and the text "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte em alguns dias.", with no AI narrative paragraph attempted.
33	3. **Given** the user has more than thirty entries, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a multi-bar ochre chart (aggregated into the chart's fixed number of buckets) and, once it loads, an AI-written summary paragraph describing the pattern.
34	4. **Given** the chart has loaded successfully for an account with data, **When** the AI narrative call fails or times out, **Then** the chart remains visible and correct, and the narrative area shows a distinct "narrativa indisponível" message rather than staying blank or showing the empty-history copy.
35	5. **Given** the user created a new entry in another screen since Settings was last open, **When** they open Settings again, **Then** the dashboard reflects the new entry in its aggregate — recomputed fresh, not read from a stale result of the previous visit.
36	6. **Given** the user has more than one entry but not enough to populate every one of the chart's ten bars (e.g. 5 or 15 entries), **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows the same multi-bar chart and narrative behavior as the "more than thirty entries" case, just with fewer of the ten bars populated — not the single-bar "Ainda é cedo..." message and not a separate, undefined state.
37	
38	---
39	
40	### User Story 2 - Deleting your account for good (Priority: P1)
41	
42	A user who wants to leave can permanently erase their account and every piece of data tied to it, with a clear, hard-to-misclick warning first, and no way to undo it afterward.
43	
44	**Why this priority**: Required by RNF05 (LGPD hard delete) — a legal and trust-critical capability, not a convenience feature. Getting this wrong (deleting too little, deleting by accident, or appearing to delete without really doing so) is a compliance and trust failure, not just a bug.
45	
46	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by tapping "Apagar conta", confirming through the destructive dialog, and verifying the account can no longer log in and the Settings screen is left entirely (no residual session), independent of any other screen.
47	
48	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
49	
50	1. **Given** the user is on Settings, **When** they tap "Apagar conta", **Then** a centered confirmation dialog appears with a red title ("Apagar sua conta?"), explanatory text that the action is permanent and irreversible, a red "Apagar tudo" button, and an outline "Cancelar" button.
51	2. **Given** the confirmation dialog is open, **When** the user taps "Cancelar", **Then** the dialog closes, no backend call is made, and Settings is otherwise unaffected.
52	3. **Given** the confirmation dialog is open, **When** the user taps "Apagar tudo", **Then** the app requests the account's permanent deletion, and on success clears all local session and account state and leaves the user at the app's authentication entry point, with no "account deleted" success screen of its own.
53	4. **Given** the deletion request fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), **When** the failure is reported, **Then** the account is left intact, the user sees a clear error, and can retry — the dialog does not falsely report success.
54	
55	---
56	
57	### User Story 3 - Signing out and managing your profile (Priority: P2)
58	
59	From the same screen, the user can see their profile, rename themselves, flip the Face ID/Touch ID unlock preference on or off, and sign out — all lower-stakes, everyday actions compared to Stories 1 and 2.
60	
61	**Why this priority**: Explicitly named in the feature's scope ("the profile and account actions that live on it") but individually lower risk and lower complexity than the dashboard or account deletion.
62	
63	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by editing the display name and confirming it persists after reopening the app, flipping the biometric toggle and confirming it is saved, and tapping "Sair" and confirming the session ends.
64	
65	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
66	
67	1. **Given** the user is on Settings, **When** the screen loads, **Then** it shows an initials avatar (52px), the current display name and email, and the editable-name control as a pencil icon.
68	2. **Given** the user taps the pencil icon next to their name, **When** the name field becomes editable, **Then** the pencil icon becomes a check icon and the email remains read-only (not editable) throughout.
69	3. **Given** the user edits their name to a valid value (1–80 characters) and taps the check icon, **When** the save request succeeds, **Then** the field returns to display mode showing the new name, and the new name is still shown after the app is restarted.
70	4. **Given** the save request fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), **When** the failure is reported, **Then** the field stays in edit mode with the user's typed text intact, a clear error is shown, and the user can retry without re-typing.
71	5. **Given** the device supports biometrics, **When** the user flips the "Face ID/Touch ID" toggle on Settings, **Then** the app saves the new preference, and the toggle reflects the saved state (or reverts with an error if the save fails).
72	6. **Given** the user taps "Sair", **When** the sign-out request completes (or fails), **Then** the local session is cleared either way, and the user lands at the app's authentication entry point with no residual access to their data.
73	
74	---
75	
76	### Edge Cases
77	
78	- The GET /dashboard/aggregate call itself fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), independent of the narrative call: the dashboard shows a clear, non-crashing error state for the chart area (distinct from the "zero entries" empty state) with a way to retry, and no narrative is requested until the aggregate succeeds.
79	- The session expires while Settings is open (dashboard loading, name being edited, or a confirmation dialog open): the existing expired-session handling (established by F000, continued by RF07) takes over exactly as it does elsewhere; re-authenticating returns the user to Settings with the dashboard, profile, and any in-progress edit reasonably re-requested, not silently lost.
80	- The user double-taps "Apagar tudo" or "Sair" before the first request resolves: this does not fire a second concurrent delete/logout request.
81	- The device has no biometric hardware or nothing enrolled: the toggle row is hidden entirely (not shown in a disabled state), rather than letting the user "turn on" something the device cannot perform.
82	- The user submits an empty name or one over 80 characters: the save is blocked client-side with a clear validation message, no request is sent, and the field stays in edit mode.
83	- Opening Settings, viewing the dashboard, editing the profile, or opening (and cancelling) the delete-confirmation dialog does not alter any other screen's state — My Records' list/filters, chat sessions, or action plans are untouched by this unit.
84	
85	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
86	
87	### Functional Requirements
88	
89	- **FR-001**: Opening Settings MUST request `GET /dashboard/aggregate` and `GET /dashboard/narrative` as two independent calls, so that a narrative failure or delay never blocks the chart from rendering with the aggregate data it already has.
90	- **FR-002**: The dashboard MUST request and render a single, fixed period and MUST NOT present a user-facing control to switch between periods in this unit — the prototype shows no such control, and only the fixed period's acceptance scenarios (zero / one / more than thirty entries) are in scope.

97	- **FR-009**: Settings MUST display the account's initials avatar, current display name, and current email (read-only) — email MUST NOT be editable in this unit, since `PATCH /account/settings` accepts no email field and rejects attempts to change it.
98	- **FR-010**: Settings MUST let the user edit their display name through an inline pencil-to-check control; saving MUST call `PATCH /account/settings` with the new `displayName` (1–80 characters) and MUST update the locally displayed/cached name on success.
99	- **FR-011**: A client-side validation MUST block submitting an empty name or one longer than 80 characters, with no backend call made and the field left in edit mode with an inline error.
100	- **FR-012**: If the name save fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), the field MUST remain in edit mode with the user's typed value intact, show a clear retryable error, and MUST NOT silently revert or discard the typed text.
101	- **FR-013**: On a device where biometrics are available, Settings MUST offer a toggle reflecting the account's current `biometricEnabled` preference and MUST let the user change it; changing it MUST call `PATCH /account/settings` with the new `biometricEnabled` value, continuing the account-settings read/write path RF03 already established for this same flag. On a device with no biometric hardware or nothing enrolled, the toggle row MUST be hidden entirely rather than shown in a disabled state.
102	- **FR-014**: If the biometric toggle save fails, the toggle MUST revert to its last-confirmed state and show a clear, retryable error, rather than appearing to succeed.
103	- **FR-015**: This unit MUST NOT build the AI persona selector ("Analítico"/"Empático"/"Socrático") or any other extension feature (requirements, section 2), even though `PATCH /account/settings` also carries a `persona` field for that extension.
104	- **FR-016**: Settings MUST offer a "Sair" action that calls `POST /auth/logout` and, regardless of whether that call succeeds or fails, MUST clear the local session and any cached account/profile state and return the user to the app's authentication entry point, with no dedicated "signed out" success screen.
105	- **FR-017**: Settings MUST offer an "Apagar conta" action (styled as destructive/red) that opens a confirmation dialog matching the prototype — red title "Apagar sua conta?", text stating the action is permanent and irreversible, a red "Apagar tudo" button, and an outline "Cancelar" button — and MUST NOT call the delete endpoint before this dialog is explicitly confirmed.
106	- **FR-018**: Confirming the dialog MUST call `DELETE /account` with the backend-required `confirmation: "DELETE"` value supplied by the app itself (the user is not asked to type the word "DELETE"; the dialog's own destructive button tap is the explicit confirmation, matching the prototype's two-button dialog with no text field).

109	- **FR-021**: Cancelling the delete-confirmation dialog MUST dismiss it without any backend call and without altering any Settings state (dashboard, profile fields, or toggle values).
110	- **FR-022**: Repeated taps on "Sair" or "Apagar tudo" before a prior request for the same action resolves MUST NOT fire a second concurrent request.

114	### Key Entities
115	
116	- **Dashboard Aggregate**: The chart data for one period — a set of date-bucketed counts (split by entry source: manual/audio/photo/chat) plus totals. Always returns a well-formed (possibly all-zero) result rather than an error for an account with no entries; recomputed fresh on every Settings visit, never persisted locally across visits.
117	- **Dashboard Narrative**: An independently-fetched, AI-generated paragraph describing the aggregate's pattern for the same period. Can succeed, fail, or be skipped (zero/one-entry scenarios) independently of whether the aggregate itself loaded successfully.

122	
123	### Measurable Outcomes
124	
125	- **SC-001**: Across accounts seeded with zero, one, and more than thirty entries, the dashboard renders the correct dedicated state in 100% of cases with zero crashes and zero mixed-up states (e.g., the empty-history message never appears alongside chart data).
126	- **SC-002**: In 100% of forced narrative-failure cases where the chart data itself loaded successfully, the chart remains fully visible and correct, with a distinct, clear explanation shown only in the narrative's place.
127	- **SC-003**: 100% of confirmed account-deletion attempts that succeed on the backend leave the device with no retained local session, cached profile, or other user data, and no path back into the account without creating a new one.
128	- **SC-004**: Zero account deletions occur without the user explicitly reaching and confirming the destructive dialog — cancelling or dismissing it never results in a deleted account.
129	- **SC-005**: A display-name edit that succeeds is still showing the new value after the app is fully restarted, in 100% of tested cases.
130	- **SC-006**: Signing out, from any state the screen can be in, always results in the user reaching the authentication entry point with no residual access, in 100% of tested cases.

132	## Assumptions
133	
134	- **Dashboard period**: The dashboard requests a single, fixed period rather than exposing a period-switching control, since neither the prototype's four Settings states nor its component library describes any period selector, tab, or chip for this screen — only the entry-count-driven states (zero / one / more-than-thirty) are depicted. # Feature Specification: P-RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard

**Feature Branch**: `011-settings-dashboard` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)

**Created**: 2026-10-24

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "P-RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard: Build the Settings screen with the evolution dashboard, and the profile and account actions that live on it. Requirement and acceptance criteria: docs/input/requirements.md, section 1, RF09; RNF05 (section 4) for account deletion. Prototype states: 'Tela 6 — Configurações' in its four dashboard variations and 'Tela 6 — Confirmar exclusão de conta' (prototype extract, section 2.6); profile name editing, 'Sair' and 'Apagar conta'. Backend: GET /dashboard/aggregate, GET /dashboard/narrative, PATCH /account/settings, DELETE /account, POST /auth/logout. Depends on: F000, RF01. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements, section 2), or change the backend."

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-10-24

- Q: What should the dashboard show for an account with more than one entry but not yet enough to fill the chart's full set of bars (e.g. 5 or 15 entries) — a state the spec's three enumerated scenarios (zero / exactly one / more than thirty) never covered? → A: Render the multi-bar chart using whatever of the ten bars the aggregate's buckets actually populate — naturally partial for a small count — and request the narrative for any count of two or more; "more than thirty" is the seed count chosen to reliably exercise a fully-populated demo chart, not a distinct functional threshold.
- Q: For the fixed `all` period, which can span anywhere from a few days to years of history, how should the backend's date-bucketed aggregate be mapped onto the chart's fixed ten bars? → A: Client-side, divide the account's full date range (date of the first entry through today) into ten roughly-equal time slices and sum the backend's per-date counts that fall within each slice to produce each bar's value.
- Q: Should the Face ID/Touch ID toggle be hidden entirely or shown-but-disabled on a device with no usable biometric capability? → A: Hidden entirely — the toggle row is omitted from Settings rather than shown in a disabled state.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Seeing your evolution dashboard (Priority: P1)

The user opens the Settings screen and sees, at a glance, a chart of how their recorded entries have built up over time, plus a short AI-written paragraph that puts that pattern into words. Whether they have no entries yet, just one, or a long history, the screen always shows something coherent rather than breaking or looking empty by accident.

**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF09 — without a correctly rendering chart and narrative, the feature does not exist. **Scope: aggregation and rendering only — the quality of the AI-written narrative text is never evaluated.**

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening Settings for accounts seeded with zero, one, and more than thirty entries respectively, and confirming each renders its own distinct, non-crashing state with the correct chart and text.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user has zero entries, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a light-gray placeholder chart icon (no chart) and the text "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui", with no AI narrative paragraph shown or requested.
2. **Given** the user has exactly one entry, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a single small bar and the text "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte em alguns dias.", with no AI narrative paragraph attempted.
3. **Given** the user has more than thirty entries, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a multi-bar ochre chart (aggregated into the chart's fixed number of buckets) and, once it loads, an AI-written summary paragraph describing the pattern.
4. **Given** the chart has loaded successfully for an account with data, **When** the AI narrative call fails or times out, **Then** the chart remains visible and correct, and the narrative area shows a distinct "narrativa indisponível" message rather than staying blank or showing the empty-history copy.
5. **Given** the user created a new entry in another screen since Settings was last open, **When** they open Settings again, **Then** the dashboard reflects the new entry in its aggregate — recomputed fresh, not read from a stale result of the previous visit.
6. **Given** the user has more than one entry but not enough to populate every one of the chart's ten bars (e.g. 5 or 15 entries), **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows the same multi-bar chart and narrative behavior as the "more than thirty entries" case, just with fewer of the ten bars populated — not the single-bar "Ainda é cedo..." message and not a separate, undefined state.

---

### User Story 2 - Deleting your account for good (Priority: P1)

A user who wants to leave can permanently erase their account and every piece of data tied to it, with a clear, hard-to-misclick warning first, and no way to undo it afterward.

**Why this priority**: Required by RNF05 (LGPD hard delete) — a legal and trust-critical capability, not a convenience feature. Getting this wrong (deleting too little, deleting by accident, or appearing to delete without really doing so) is a compliance and trust failure, not just a bug.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by tapping "Apagar conta", confirming through the destructive dialog, and verifying the account can no longer log in and the Settings screen is left entirely (no residual session), independent of any other screen.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user is on Settings, **When** they tap "Apagar conta", **Then** a centered confirmation dialog appears with a red title ("Apagar sua conta?"), explanatory text that the action is permanent and irreversible, a red "Apagar tudo" button, and an outline "Cancelar" button.
2. **Given** the confirmation dialog is open, **When** the user taps "Cancelar", **Then** the dialog closes, no backend call is made, and Settings is otherwise unaffected.
3. **Given** the confirmation dialog is open, **When** the user taps "Apagar tudo", **Then** the app requests the account's permanent deletion, and on success clears all local session and account state and leaves the user at the app's authentication entry point, with no "account deleted" success screen of its own.
4. **Given** the deletion request fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), **When** the failure is reported, **Then** the account is left intact, the user sees a clear error, and can retry — the dialog does not falsely report success.

---

### User Story 3 - Signing out and managing your profile (Priority: P2)

From the same screen, the user can see their profile, rename themselves, flip the Face ID/Touch ID unlock preference on or off, and sign out — all lower-stakes, everyday actions compared to Stories 1 and 2.

3. **Given** the user edits their name to a valid value (1–80 characters) and taps the check icon, **When** the save request succeeds, **Then** the field returns to display mode showing the new name, and the new name is still shown after the app is restarted.
4. **Given** the save request fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), **When** the failure is reported, **Then** the field stays in edit mode with the user's typed text intact, a clear error is shown, and the user can retry without re-typing.
5. **Given** the device supports biometrics, **When** the user flips the "Face ID/Touch ID" toggle on Settings, **Then** the app saves the new preference, and the toggle reflects the saved state (or reverts with an error if the save fails).
6. **Given** the user taps "Sair", **When** the sign-out request completes (or fails), **Then** the local session is cleared either way, and the user lands at the app's authentication entry point with no residual access to their data.

This unit treats the most recent such response (including ones written by RF03's first-time biometric setup) as the locally cached source of truth for what Settings displays, with a sensible default (e.g., a name derived from the email's local part) for an account whose profile has never been successfully written.
- **Email is read-only despite the prototype's pencil icon**: The prototype extract describes "editable name/e-mail" with a shared pencil-to-check control, but the frozen API contract's `PATCH /account/settings` accepts no `email` field and explicitly rejects email changes. Per the requirements document's own rule ("where this differs from the API contract, the contract prevails"), this unit treats only the display name as editable and shows the email as plain, read-only text.
- **No typed "DELETE" confirmation text field**: The backend requires the literal request field `confirmation: "DELETE"`, but the prototype's confirmation dialog shows only a title, explanatory text, and two buttons — no text input. This unit treats the destructive button tap itself as the required explicit confirmation and supplies the literal value in the request automatically, without asking the user to type anything.
- **Where "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" land**: The prototype extract states both actions return to the "Biometria" screen with no dedicated success screen of their own. Since both actions end with no stored session, and F000 already routes a device with no stored session to the login/sign-up screen on next launch, this unit treats "the app's authentication entry point" as whatever F000/RF03 already resolve that case to (the vault screen if a device-level PIN/biometric flow applies with no session, falling through to login otherwise) rather than building a separate destination.
- **Biometric toggle is in scope, persona is not**: RF03's own specification explicitly defers the biometric on/off toggle (outside of first-time setup) to "the Settings screen built by the RF09 unit." The persona selector, by contrast, is explicitly listed as a non-implemented extension feature (requirements, section 2) even though both preferences share the same `PATCH /account/settings` endpoint.
- **Chart's fixed bucket count and bucketing algorithm**: The chart always has ten bars (the prototype's reference mock). For the fixed `all` period — which can span anywhere from a few days to years of account history — this unit divides the account's full date range (date of the first entry through today) into ten roughly-equal time slices and sums the aggregate's per-date `count` values falling within each slice to produce each bar's value. An account whose history is short or clustered naturally produces a chart with some empty bars rather than this being treated as a defect; this unit does not need to support an arbitrary, unbounded number of visible bars.
- **Multi-bar chart applies to any count above one, not only "more than thirty"**: FR-005's chart-and-narrative state is not gated on a literal minimum entry count beyond "two or more" — an account with, say, 5 or 15 entries gets the same multi-bar chart (naturally sparser) and narrative request as a 30+ entry account. The "more than thirty entries" acceptance scenario exists only to guarantee a chart where every one of the ten bars is populated, for a clean, unambiguous test case — not because counts between two and thirty are a separate, unspecified state.

# Implementation Plan: P-RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard

**Branch**: `011-settings-dashboard` (spec directory only — no git branch exists; none of this repo's
extension hooks are configured, per spec.md's own header)

**Date**: 2026-10-24 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/011-settings-dashboard/spec.md`, `docs/input/requirements.md`
§1 (RF09), §4 (RNF05), §6.6–6.7 (`dashboard-aggregate-get`/`dashboard-narrative-get`/`account-settings-update`/
`account-delete`), §6.1 (`auth-logout`), §8 (data model reference), §9 (stack), §13; `docs/input/backend/api/
openapi.yaml`'s `/dashboard/*`, `/account*`, `/auth/logout` schemas; `docs/input/backend/README.md`'s
function-name mapping; `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`; `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`
§2.6, §6; and `.specify/memory/constitution.md`. Depends on F000 (session, login, routing) and RF01 (entries
exist to aggregate), both already implemented. This is the unit that replaces `SettingsPlaceholderPage` (the
route `AppRoutes.settings` already points at a static "Ainda não disponível." placeholder) with the real
screen, and that finally wires in the real display name `app_drawer.dart`'s own stand-in email-derivation
comment has been waiting for since F000.

## Summary

The Settings screen (`AppRoutes.settings`, currently `SettingsPlaceholderPage`) becomes a real, four-concern
screen backed by one screen-scoped `SettingsBloc`: (1) an evolution dashboard — `GET /dashboard/aggregate` and
`GET /dashboard/narrative` as two independent calls, the aggregate's ten-bar chart built by a new pure
derivation (`DashboardAggregate.tenBars()`, research.md R2) and rendered with plain `Container`-based bars
(no new charting dependency, research.md R3); (2) an editable profile header (52px initials avatar, inline
pencil-to-check name editing via `PATCH /account/settings`, read-only email) backed by a new, narrow
`AccountProfileRepository` whose confirmed writes persist into a new `AccountProfileLocalCache`
(`features/settings/data/`, Keychain-backed) — the one local mirror this unit adds, since no earlier unit
ever wrote `displayName`; (3) a biometrics toggle that is hidden entirely on a device with no usable
capability and otherwise reuses RF03's own `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`/`VaultRepository` as-is behind a
new, settings-owned, await-then-revert usecase (research.md R6) rather than RF03's deliberately
fire-and-forget one; (4) "Sair" (extends the existing `AuthRepository` with one new method, `logout()`) and
"Apagar conta" (a new `AccountDeletionRepository`, `DELETE /account`), both ending in the same
clear-local-state-and-navigate sequence spec.md's own Assumptions resolve to the existing vault/login routes
(research.md R10) — deletion alone additionally wipes `EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache` (both extended in
place with a new `clear()` method) since "any other locally held user data" (FR-019) is a strictly wider
clear than logout's own FR-016 wording. `app_drawer.dart` is extended in place to read the same cached display
name (research.md R13), and `SettingsPage` becomes `RouteAware` on the already-existing `chatRouteObserver` so
re-authenticating mid-screen re-requests fresh data rather than only preserving stale state (research.md R15).

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Dart 3.13.4 / Flutter 3.47.5 (stable), pinned via `.fvmrc` — unchanged from every prior
unit.

**Primary Dependencies**: None added. Reuses the full existing stack — `flutter_bloc`, `fpdart`, `get_it`,
`equatable`, `dio` (via `ApiClient`, no new method needed — every call here is a plain JSON `call()`, the same
shape `BiometricsPreferenceRemoteDataSource` already uses), `flutter_secure_storage` (via a new
`AccountProfileLocalCache`, same pattern as `VaultSecureStorage`/`EntriesLocalCache`), `local_auth` (indirectly,
through the unmodified `VaultRepository`), `go_router` (no new route — `AppRoutes.settings` already exists;
only its builder changes); dev-only `mocktail`, `bloc_test`. Research.md R3 explicitly rejects adding a
charting package — the 10-bar chart is plain `Container`s.

**Storage**: One new on-device key, `AccountProfileLocalCache`'s single `settingsDisplayName` Keychain entry
(research.md R5/R7) — the only new local persistence this unit introduces. `DashboardAggregate`/
`DashboardNarrative` are explicitly never persisted (FR-008 — "recomputed fresh... never served from a result
cached from a previous visit"), unlike `EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache`'s own cross-restart caches.

**Testing**: `flutter_test` + `bloc_test` + `mocktail`, unchanged tooling. Coverage via `fvm flutter test
--coverage`, same `lib/**/domain/**` lcov filter (RNF07), now additionally exercising
`DashboardAggregate.tenBars()`'s pure bucketing (research.md R2 — the single richest piece of new domain
logic this unit adds, mirroring `DateRangeFilter`/`SyncBadgeState`'s existing pure-derivation test shape),
`AccountProfile.isValidDisplayName`/`.initials`/`.defaultDisplayNameFromEmail`, and
`SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase`'s await-then-mirror-or-revert branches (contracts/
biometric-preference-settings-extension.md) against `mocktail` fakes of `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`/
`VaultRepository` — no new fakes needed for `local_auth`/`flutter_secure_storage` themselves, since neither is
touched directly by anything new.

**Target Platform**: iOS, portrait only — unchanged. No native project file touched; no new package needs an
iOS install step.

**Project Type**: Same single Flutter mobile app. One new feature folder, `lib/features/settings/`
(domain/data/presentation, Principle V) replacing the one-file `SettingsPlaceholderPage` (deleted); three
existing files extended in place — `lib/features/auth/domain/repositories/auth_repository.dart` (+
`data`/`impl`, + `logout()`), `lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` (+ `impl`, +
`clearLocalData()`), `lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart` (+ `impl`, +
`clearLocalData()`) — plus their respective local caches (`EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache`) each gaining a
new `clear()` method; `lib/features/home/presentation/widgets/app_drawer.dart` (display-name read, research.md
R13); `lib/core/routing/app_router.dart` (`AppRoutes.settings`'s builder); `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (5 new
tokens, research.md R14); `lib/core/di/service_locator.dart`. No backend/server code, no change to
`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`.

**Performance Goals**: RNF01 unchanged. The optimistic UI flips this unit adds — the biometric toggle's
immediate visual change before its network write resolves, and the name field's immediate return to display
mode is deliberately *not* optimistic (it waits for the `Right`, since a wrong optimistic name could be shown
then silently reverted, worse than a brief wait) — reflect within 100ms where used; every network call in
this unit's flow (dashboard load, name save, toggle save, sign-out, deletion) already has a loading indicator
by construction (`dashboardStatus == loading`, `nameEditStatus == saving`, `biometricSaving`, `isSigningOut`,
`isDeletingAccount` each drive one), satisfying the >300ms affordance requirement.

**Constraints**:
- No period-switching UI control (FR-002) — the dashboard always requests the fixed `period=all`.
- No AI persona selector or any other extension feature (FR-015) — `account-settings-update`'s `persona`
  field is never sent by this unit's requests and never read from its responses.
- No functionality belonging to a unit later than RF09 in the build order, and no backend/contract/config
  change (FR-024) — every endpoint this unit calls is one `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml` already
  documents, called exactly as documented (contracts/*.md's own request-shape listings).
- Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature (Principle V) — `settings/domain/` imports only `equatable`/
  `fpdart`/`core/network/failure.dart`; `SettingsBloc` depends on `settings/domain/` repositories/usecases plus
  two other features' already-domain-layer interfaces (`vault/domain/`'s `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`/
  `VaultRepository`, `auth/domain/`'s `AuthRepository`, `session/domain/`'s `SessionRepository`,
  `entries/domain/`'s `EntriesRepository`, `chat/domain/`'s `ChatRepository`) — never any other feature's
  `presentation/bloc/` (enforced by `test/architecture/no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart`, unmodified, which
  already scans every `presentation/bloc/` path recursively).
- FR-022's concurrency guard is satisfied by `SettingsState`'s own `isSigningOut`/`isDeletingAccount` booleans
  (research.md R12), not a shared/persisted flag — the same shape `ExportBloc`'s own tap-guard already uses.
- Zero visual values hardcoded outside `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (Principle IV/RNF08) — the 5 genuinely
  new values this unit needs (data-model.md's token table, research.md R14) are added there, not inlined.

**Scale/Scope**: 1 new feature folder (`settings/`) with 4 domain entities + 1 pure bucketing extension, 3
repository interfaces + 1 reused usecase pattern (1 new settings-owned usecase), 3 data classes (2 remote data
sources + 1 local cache) + 3 repository impls, 1 bloc (+events/states), ~7 new presentation widgets; 3
existing features' interfaces each extended by exactly one method (+ impl); 2 existing local caches each
gaining a `clear()` method; 1 existing widget (`app_drawer.dart`) extended in place; 1 deleted file
(`settings_placeholder_page.dart`); 5 new `DesignTokens` values; ~14 new DI registrations.

## Constitution Check

Every technical-judgment decision this plan makes (R1–R16, research.md) is built directly on spec.md's own FRs/Clarifications/Assumptions/Edge-Cases wording — the data-flow split (R1), the bucketing arithmetic (R2), the no-new-dependency chart (R3), the flat composite state shape (R4), the per-field caching split (R5), the biometric await-revert usecase (R6), the narrow display-name repository (R7), the logout/deletion homing (R8), the clear-scope split (R9), the post-action destination (R10), the reauth-stream wiring (R11), the concurrency guards (R12), the extracted email-derivation (R13), the 5 new tokens (R14), the `RouteAware` post-reauth refresh (R15) — none reopens a resolved Clarification. |

  import of `entries/domain/usecases/create_entry_usecase.dart` already establishes, not a new, unprecedented
  presentation-reaches-into-another-feature's-data shape.

No new violations. Gate remains PASS.

572

574	2. Complete Phase 2: Foundational (CRITICAL — blocks everything).
575	3. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1.

579	
580	### Incremental Delivery

583	2. Add User Story 1 → validate independently → the dashboard is live (MVP).
584	3. Add User Story 2 → validate independently → "Apagar conta" is live, RNF05's compliance gate satisfied.

# Tasks: P-RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/011-settings-dashboard/`
**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md (all present)

**Tests**: Not explicitly requested in spec.md beyond the constitutional RNF07 (≥80% domain coverage) and
RNF09 (full `Either`/scenario-table coverage) gates, which this project's every prior unit has satisfied with
real `flutter_test`/`bloc_test`/`mocktail` tests (not skipped). Test tasks are therefore included, scoped
exactly to what research.md/contracts/*.md's own scenario tables enumerate — no broader test suite than that.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story (US1 = dashboard, US2 = account deletion, US3 =
profile/biometric/sign-out) per spec.md's own priority order (US1 = P1, US2 = P1, US3 = P2). Foundational
work shared by all three stories (entities, the two existing-feature extensions, DI, tokens) is Phase 2.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependencies)
- **[Story]**: US1 (dashboard), US2 (account deletion), US3 (profile/biometric/sign-out)
- Every file path is exact; every entity/field constraint is quoted from data-model.md/contracts/*.md verbatim
  where one exists.

## Path Conventions

Single Flutter mobile project. New feature folder: `lib/features/settings/{domain,data,presentation}/`.
Tests mirror under `test/features/settings/` and `test/features/{auth,entries,chat,home}/` for the three
extended-in-place files, following this repo's existing `test/features/<feature>/<layer>/...` convention.

---

## Phase 1: Setup

No new dependencies, no new project scaffolding beyond the feature folder structure itself (plan.md Technical
Context: "No primary dependencies added"). This phase only creates the directory skeleton; no file content.

- [ ] T001 Create the empty `lib/features/settings/domain/entities/`, `lib/features/settings/domain/repositories/`,
  `lib/features/settings/domain/usecases/`, `lib/features/settings/data/`,
  `lib/features/settings/presentation/bloc/`, `lib/features/settings/presentation/widgets/` directories
  (`lib/features/settings/presentation/pages/` already exists, holding `settings_placeholder_page.dart`)

---

## Phase 2: Foundational (Blocking Prerequisites)

**Purpose**: Domain entities, design tokens, and the three existing-feature extensions (`auth`, `entries`,
`chat`) that every user story's implementation phase depends on, plus DI wiring for everything not already
registered. **⚠️ CRITICAL**: No user story phase can be completed until this phase is done — `SettingsBloc`
(built across all three story phases) depends on every repository/usecase interface defined here.

### Design tokens

- [ ] T002 [P] Add 5 new `DesignTokens` values to `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (research.md R14,
  data-model.md): `static const double sizeAvatarSettings = 52;` (prototype-extract.md §6, "52px in
  Configurações"), `static const double sizeChartBarMaxHeight = 120;`, `static const double
  sizeChartBarWidth = 20;`, `static const double sizeChartBarGap = 6;` (Sizes section), and `static const
  Color colorChartPlaceholder = Color(0xFFE1DACB);` (Colors section — same hex as existing `colorBorder`,
  added under a new, semantically distinct name)

### Domain entities (`lib/features/settings/domain/entities/`)

- [ ] T003 [P] Create `DashboardSourceCounts` (`{manual, audio, photo, chat}`, each `int`, each "≥ 0"
  data-model.md), `AggregateBucket` (`{date: DateTime, count: int, sources: DashboardSourceCounts}` — "Parsed
  from the backend's `YYYY-MM-DD` string, date-only (no time component kept)", "count ≥ 0"), and
  `DashboardTotals` (`{count: int, sources: DashboardSourceCounts}`) in
  `lib/features/settings/domain/entities/dashboard_aggregate.dart`, each `Equatable`
- [ ] T004 [P] Create `DashboardAggregate` (`{buckets: List<AggregateBucket>, totals: DashboardTotals}`,
  `Equatable`) with the pure method `List<int> tenBars({DateTime? today})` in
  `lib/features/settings/domain/entities/dashboard_aggregate.dart`, implementing the exact algorithm from
  research.md R2: if `buckets.isEmpty` return `List.filled(10, 0)`; else compute `start` as the earliest
  bucket date, `totalDaySpan = (today ?? DateTime.now()).difference(start).inDays`; if `totalDaySpan == 0`,
  put the full summed count in `bars[9]`; otherwise for each bucket compute `index = (daysSinceStart * 10) ~/
  (totalDaySpan + 1)` clamped to `[0, 9]` and accumulate `count` into `bars[index]`
- [ ] T005 [P] Create `DashboardNarrative` (`{text: String, generatedAt: DateTime}`, `Equatable`) in
  `lib/features/settings/domain/entities/dashboard_narrative.dart`
- [ ] T006 [P] Create `AccountProfile` (`{displayName: String, email: String}`, `Equatable`) in
  `lib/features/settings/domain/entities/account_profile.dart` with: `static String
  defaultDisplayNameFromEmail(String email)` — relocate `app_drawer.dart`'s existing
  `_displayNameFromEmail`/`_emailNameWords` logic byte-for-byte unchanged (splits the email's local part on
  `._-`, title-cases each word, joins with a space; returns `email` itself if the local part is empty,

---

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: No dependencies — can start immediately.
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup. Blocks all three user story phases — every story's
  `SettingsBloc` work depends on the entities/repository interfaces/usecase/extensions defined here.
- **User Story 1 (Phase 3)**: Depends on Phase 2. Also creates the shared `settings_event.dart`/
  `settings_state.dart`/`settings_bloc.dart`/`settings_page.dart` files that Phases 4 and 5 extend in place.
- **User Story 2 (Phase 4)**: Depends on Phase 2 and on Phase 3's creation of `settings_bloc.dart`/
  `settings_page.dart` (it extends those files rather than creating new ones) — cannot start in true
  parallel with Phase 3 on those shared files, though its own new files (T038, T039, T042) can be built
  ahead of time.
- **User Story 3 (Phase 5)**: Same shared-file dependency on Phase 3 as Phase 4; independent of Phase 4's
  own new files otherwise.
- **Polish (Phase 6)**: Depends on Phases 3, 4, and 5 all being complete.

### User Story Dependencies

- **US1**: No dependency on US2/US3's own logic — the dashboard section is fully self-contained once Phase
  2 is done.
- **US2**: No functional dependency on US1 beyond sharing `settings_bloc.dart`/`settings_page.dart` as files
  (the delete flow reads no dashboard state).
- **US3**: No functional dependency on US1/US2 beyond the same shared files; profile/biometric/sign-out
  logic is independent of both.

### Within Each User Story

- Tests before implementation where both exist for the same unit of work.
- Data sources before repository impls; repository impls before bloc handlers; bloc handlers before widgets
  that dispatch their events; widgets before the page that assembles them; DI registration last (needs the
  concrete classes to exist).

### Parallel Opportunities

- All Phase 2 entity tasks (T003–T006) are `[P]` — different files, no interdependency beyond T004 extending
  the same file T003 creates (sequential within that one file, parallel with T005/T006).
- All Phase 2 repository-interface tasks (T007–T009) are `[P]`.
- The three existing-feature extension tracks (`auth`: T011→T012→T013; `entries`: T014/T015→T016; `chat`:
  T017/T018→T019) are mutually `[P]` as tracks, sequential within each track.
- T020/T021 (foundational tests) are `[P]`.
- Within US1: T023/T024 (tests, same file but independent scenario groups — write together), T025 alongside
  T027/T028 are `[P]`; T030/T031/T032 (three independent widget files) are `[P]`.
- Within US2: T036/T037 are `[P]`; T042 is `[P]` with the bloc-handler work (T041).
- Within US3: T045/T046/T047 are `[P]`; T049/T050 are `[P]`; T055/T056 are `[P]`.

---

## Parallel Example: Phase 2 Foundational

```bash
# Launch independent entity/repository-interface creation together:
Task: "Create DashboardSourceCounts/AggregateBucket/DashboardTotals in dashboard_aggregate.dart"
Task: "Create DashboardNarrative in dashboard_narrative.dart"
Task: "Create AccountProfile in account_profile.dart"
Task: "Create DashboardRepository interface"
Task: "Create AccountProfileRepository interface"
Task: "Create AccountDeletionRepository interface"

# Launch the three independent existing-feature-extension tracks together:
Task: "auth: add logout() to AuthRepository interface"
Task: "entries: add clear() to EntriesLocalCache"
Task: "chat: add clear() to ChatLocalCache"
```

## Parallel Example: User Story 1

```bash
Task: "Test DashboardRepositoryImpl.fetchAggregate() scenarios"
Task: "Test DashboardRepositoryImpl.fetchNarrative() scenarios"

Task: "Create DashboardBarChart widget"
Task: "Create DashboardCard widget"
Task: "Create NarrativeView widget"
```

---

## Implementation Strategy

### MVP First (User Story 1 Only)

1. Complete Phase 1: Setup.
2. Complete Phase 2: Foundational (CRITICAL — blocks everything).
3. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1.
4. **STOP and VALIDATE**: Run quickstart.md Story 1's five numbered checks against accounts A–D.
5. Settings now shows a correct, real dashboard in place of the placeholder — a demoable increment even
   before account deletion or profile editing exist.

### Incremental Delivery

1. Setup + Foundational → shared foundation ready.
2. Add User Story 1 → validate independently → the dashboard is live (MVP).
3. Add User Story 2 → validate independently → "Apagar conta" is live, RNF05's compliance gate satisfied.
4. Add User Story 3 → validate independently → profile editing, biometrics, and "Sair" complete the screen.
5. Phase 6 polish (placeholder deletion, architecture re-checks, coverage, full quickstart) closes the unit.

### Parallel Team Strategy

With multiple developers, once Phase 2 is done: one developer takes US1 (and creates the shared bloc/page
files), while a second prepares US2's and a third prepares US3's own new files (data sources, repository
impls, widgets) ahead of time — the only serialization point is each one's final bloc-handler/page-wiring
task (T041/T043, T054/T057), which must land after Phase 3's T029/T033 exist.

---

## Notes

- [P] tasks = different files, no dependencies.
- [Story] label maps task to US1/US2/US3 for traceability; Foundational/Setup/Polish tasks carry none.
- `settings_event.dart`, `settings_state.dart`, `settings_bloc.dart`, and `settings_page.dart` are each
  created once (Phase 3) and extended in place by Phases 4 and 5 — not recreated.
- Verify tests fail before implementing, where tests are written first.
- Commit after each task or logical group.
- Stop at any checkpoint to validate a story independently.
- Avoid: vague tasks, same-file conflicts within a single phase's `[P]` group, cross-story dependencies that
  would break independent testability.

# Contract: `DashboardRepository`

`features/settings/domain/repositories/dashboard_repository.dart`, implemented by
`DashboardRepositoryImpl` (`features/settings/data/`), backed by `DashboardRemoteDataSource` calling
`dashboard-aggregate-get` (`GET /dashboard/aggregate?period=all`) and `dashboard-narrative-get`
(`GET /dashboard/narrative?period=all`).

```dart
abstract class DashboardRepository {
  Future<Either<Failure, DashboardAggregate>> fetchAggregate();
  Future<Either<Failure, DashboardNarrative>> fetchNarrative();
}
```

## Parsing

`fetchAggregate()` decodes `data.buckets[]` (`date`, `count`, `sources.{manual,audio,photo,chat}`) and
`data.totals` (`count`, `sources`) per `openapi.yaml`'s schema (both always present, even for a zero-entry
account — "always 200" per the contract's own summary line). `fetchNarrative()` decodes `data.text`/
`data.generatedAt`. A missing/mistyped required field on either call is a `ValidationFailure` (`TypeError`
caught, never thrown past this boundary — same pattern as `SessionRepositoryImpl._assembleFromCheckSession`).

## Retry-once-on-expiry

Both methods follow `EntriesRepositoryImpl._retryAfterSilentRefresh`'s exact shape: on `AuthExpiredFailure`,
call `SessionRepository.refresh()` once; on its own failure, return
`Left(AuthExpiredFailure(message: 'Session could not be renewed'))` (no second refresh attempt); on success,
retry the original call exactly once more and return whatever it resolves to.

## Scenario table (RNF09 — `fetchAggregate`/`fetchNarrative` are `GET`s, outside the write-endpoint tally,
but still fully `Either`-typed and tested)

| # | Scenario | Expected `Either` |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 200, zero-entry account (`buckets: []`, `totals.count: 0`) | `Right(DashboardAggregate)` with an empty bucket list — never a `Left` |
| 2 | 200, well-formed non-empty payload | `Right(DashboardAggregate)` / `Right(DashboardNarrative)` |
| 3 | Dio timeout | `Left(NetworkTimeoutFailure)` |
| 4 | No connection (no response) | `Left(NetworkOfflineFailure)` |
| 5 | 200 with a malformed body (`buckets` not a list / `count` missing) | `Left(ValidationFailure)` |
| 6 | 401 `AUTH_EXPIRED`, silent refresh succeeds | retried call's own result (success path re-exercises #1/#2) |
| 7 | 401 `AUTH_EXPIRED`, silent refresh itself fails | `Left(AuthExpiredFailure)`, and `SettingsBloc.reauthRequired` fires |
| 8 | `dashboard-narrative-get` returns `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | `Left(AiGenerationTimeoutFailure)` — mapped by `ErrorMapper` unchanged, surfaced by `SettingsBloc` as the "narrativa indisponível" state (FR-006), never conflated with #1's empty-history copy |

## `DashboardAggregate.tenBars()` — see data-model.md / research.md R2

Exercised directly by a domain unit test (no repository/network involved) for: empty input (10 zeros), a
single bucket on "today" (all weight in bar 9), buckets spanning exactly 10 days (one bucket per bar,
1:1), buckets spanning 100 days (several buckets folding into the same bar), and a bucket dated after `today`

# Contract: Sign-out (`AuthRepository.logout()` extension) + shared post-action destination

## `AuthRepository.logout()` — extends an existing interface (research.md R8)

`features/auth/domain/repositories/auth_repository.dart` gains one method, implemented by
`AuthRepositoryImpl` via a new `AuthRemoteDataSource.logout()` calling `auth-logout` (`POST /auth/logout`,
`bearerAuth`, empty body):

```dart
Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> logout();
```

`auth-logout`'s own response is `{data: {ok: true}}`; this method returns `Right(unit)` on 200 regardless of
the `ok` value's content (unlike `account-delete`, a non-`true` `ok` here is not treated as a malformed
response worth blocking on — FR-016 already says the local session is cleared "regardless of whether that
call succeeds or fails"). `AuthRepositoryImpl.logout()` does **not** call `SecureTokenStorage`/
`SessionRepository.clear()` itself — that stays `SettingsBloc`'s job (below), so `AuthRepository` keeps its
existing shape (it has never owned session-clearing; `AuthRepositoryImpl._persistOnSuccess` only ever writes,
never deletes).

## `SettingsBloc`'s sign-out sequence (FR-016)

```
on SignOutRequested, if isSigningOut: ignore (FR-022)
set isSigningOut = true
await authRepository.logout()        // result intentionally discarded either way
await sessionRepository.clear()
await accountProfileRepository.clearCachedDisplayName()
destination = hasPinConfigured() ? vault : login   // research.md R10
emit SettingsState(..., signedOutDestination: destination)
```
Note the `logout()` call's `Either` is awaited (so the request actually completes before local state is
wiped — avoiding a race where the app's own token is already gone when the request tries to attach it) but
never branched on; both `Left` and `Right` fall through to the same unconditional clear-and-navigate sequence
this is the one place in this unit's bloc logic where a `Left` is deliberately not surfaced as an error, per
FR-016's own explicit wording.

## Scenario table

| # | Scenario | Local state after | Navigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `logout()` → `Right`, PIN configured | Session + cached name cleared | `AppRoutes.vault` |
| 2 | `logout()` → `Right`, no PIN configured (should not occur post-RF03, but not assumed impossible) | Session + cached name cleared | `AppRoutes.login` |
| 3 | `logout()` → `Left` (timeout/offline/`AUTH_EXPIRED`/malformed) | Session + cached name cleared regardless | Same as #1/#2 — failure never blocks the clear-and-leave sequence |
| 4 | A second `SignOutRequested` arrives while `isSigningOut == true` | No second `logout()` call (FR-022) | No second navigation |

`EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache` are **not** cleared on sign-out (research.md R9) — only
`AccountDeletionRepository`'s success path (contracts/account-deletion-repository.md) does that.

1	# Contract: `AccountDeletionRepository`
2	
3	`features/settings/domain/repositories/account_deletion_repository.dart`, implemented by
4	`AccountDeletionRepositoryImpl` (`features/settings/data/`), backed by
5	`AccountDeletionRemoteDataSource` calling `account-delete` (`DELETE /account`).
6	
7	```dart
8	abstract class AccountDeletionRepository {
9	  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> deleteAccount();
10	}
11	```
12	
13	## Behavior
14	
15	Always sends `{"confirmation": "DELETE"}` — the literal value the backend requires, supplied by the app
16	itself (FR-018); there is no caller-supplied parameter for it, so it is structurally impossible for this
17	method to ever send anything else. No retry-on-`AuthExpiredFailure` here: an expired session during the
18	delete-confirmation dialog is exactly spec.md's own Edge Case ("the session expires while Settings is open...
19	a confirmation dialog open") — the existing expired-session overlay takes over and the user re-authenticates
20	before retrying the tap, rather than this method silently refreshing and re-sending a destructive request
21	behind an overlay the user hasn't acknowledged yet. A plain `AuthExpiredFailure` `Left` surfaces through
22	`SettingsState.deleteFailureMessage` like any other failure and also fires `reauthRequired`.
23	
24	## What `SettingsBloc` does around a `Right` result (research.md R9) — not this repository's job
25	
26	On `Right(unit)`: `SessionRepository.clear()`, `AccountProfileLocalCache.clearCachedDisplayName()`,
27	`EntriesRepository.clearLocalData()`, `ChatRepository.clearLocalData()`, then resolve
28	`accountDeletedDestination` via `VaultRepository.hasPinConfigured()` (research.md R10). `VaultSecureStorage`'s
29	PIN hash and biometrics-preference mirror are deliberately **not** touched (research.md R9/R10).
30	
31	## Scenario table (RNF09 — new write endpoint)
32	
33	| # | Scenario | Expected `Either` | Account state after |
34	|---|---|---|---|
35	| 1 | 200 `{data: {ok: true}}` | `Right(unit)` | Backend account gone; app clears local state (above) |
36	| 2 | Dio timeout | `Left(NetworkTimeoutFailure)` | Untouched — dialog shows retryable error (FR-020) |
37	| 3 | No connection | `Left(NetworkOfflineFailure)` | Untouched |
38	| 4 | 200 with a malformed body (`data.ok` missing/not `true`) | `Left(ValidationFailure)` | Untouched — never reports success on an ambiguous response |
39	| 5 | 401 `AUTH_EXPIRED` | `Left(AuthExpiredFailure)`, `reauthRequired` fires | Untouched |
40	
41	## `SettingsBloc`'s own guard around this call (FR-022)
42	
43	`isDeletingAccount` is checked and set to `true` before the call; a second `DeleteAccountConfirmed` event
44	while it is already `true` is dropped without calling this repository a second time (research.md R12) — same
45	shape as the `isSigningOut` guard around `AuthRepository.logout()`.
46

129	
130	FR-016 (Sair): "clear the local session and any cached account/profile state." FR-019 (Apagar conta): "clear
131	all local session, cached account/profile, **and any other locally held user data**." The extra clause in
132	FR-019 is read literally as a scope difference, not a wording accident — deleting the account is the LGPD hard

136	- **Both** actions clear `SessionRepository` (`SecureTokenStorage`'s 4 keys) and `AccountProfileLocalCache`

141	- **Neither** action touches `VaultSecureStorage` (the device PIN hash or the biometrics-preference mirror) —
142	  see R10, this is deliberate and matches the prototype's own simulated destination.

149	PIN/biometric flow applies with no session, falling through to login otherwise) rather than building a
150	separate destination." The literal, minimal reading of that: `SettingsBloc` checks
151	`VaultRepository.hasPinConfigured()` after the session/profile clear and resolves to `AppRoutes.vault` (if

- **Only account deletion** additionally clears `EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache` (both extended in place
  with a new `clear()` method, R14) and their owning repositories' in-memory mirrors (`EntriesRepository`/
  `ChatRepository` gain a `clearLocalData()` method each) — "any other locally held user data," FR-019.
- **Neither** action touches `VaultSecureStorage` (the device PIN hash or the biometrics-preference mirror) —
  see R10, this is deliberate and matches the prototype's own simulated destination.

## R10 — Post-logout/deletion destination: computed from `hasPinConfigured()`, reusing existing routes only

The prototype extract states both "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" return to "Tela 0.1 — Biometria" — the same
destination (`prototype-extract.md` §1, §4.2). Spec.md's own Assumption resolves "the app's authentication
entry point" as "whatever F000/RF03 already resolve that case to (the vault screen if a device-level
PIN/biometric flow applies with no session, falling through to login otherwise) rather than building a
separate destination." The literal, minimal reading of that: `SettingsBloc` checks
`VaultRepository.hasPinConfigured()` after the session/profile clear and resolves to `AppRoutes.vault` (if
true) or `AppRoutes.login` (if false) — the same two routes `SplashPage` already builds its own routing
decision from, never a new route or screen. `SettingsPage` performs `context.go()` (not `push`) on the
resulting terminal state, discarding the whole Home/Settings back-stack, so there is no way to navigate back
into a signed-out Settings screen. Whatever happens *after* a vault unlock with no stored session (i.e.
arriving at Home with nothing to authenticate it) is explicitly left to the already-existing, already-built
expired-session machinery named in spec.md's own Edge Cases ("the existing expired-session handling —
established by F000, continued by RF07 — takes over exactly as it does elsewhere") — this unit does not add a
second mechanism for that.

`SettingsBloc` exposes a broadcast `Stream<void> get reauthRequired`, fired whenever a repository call's single
silent-refresh retry (the same `_retryAfterSilentRefresh` shape `EntriesRepositoryImpl`/`ChatRepositoryImpl`
already use) still comes back `AuthExpiredFailure`. `SettingsPage` subscribes in `initState` and forwards to
`context.read<SessionBloc>().add(const AuthExpiredDetected())` — verbatim the same wiring `RecordsPage`/

already-wired, app-level `BlocListener<SessionBloc>` in `main.dart` is what actually raises the overlay; this
unit adds no second overlay-raising mechanism.

FR-022 is satisfied the same way `ExportBloc`'s own tap-guard already is: `isSigningOut`/`isDeletingAccount`
booleans on `SettingsState`, checked at the top of the corresponding event handler before any repository call
is made — a second tap while one is `true` is a no-op. No new synchronization primitive, no shared mutable
flag outside the bloc's own state.

# Contract: `AccountProfileRepository`

`features/settings/domain/repositories/account_profile_repository.dart`, implemented by
`AccountProfileRepositoryImpl` (`features/settings/data/`), backed by
`AccountSettingsRemoteDataSource.updateDisplayName()` (`PATCH account-settings-update`, body
`{"displayName": name}` only) and `AccountProfileLocalCache` (Keychain-backed, one key,
`flutter_secure_storage`, same pattern as `VaultSecureStorage`).

```dart
abstract class AccountProfileRepository {
  Future<String?> readCachedDisplayName();
  Future<Either<Failure, String>> updateDisplayName(String name);
  Future<void> clearCachedDisplayName();
}
```

## Behavior

- `readCachedDisplayName()` — local-only, no network, no `Either` (nothing here can fail in a way the caller
  must branch on beyond "was it ever set").
- `updateDisplayName(name)` — client-side validation (`AccountProfile.isValidDisplayName`) happens in
  `SettingsBloc` *before* this is called, per FR-011 ("no backend call is made"); this method itself always
  sends the request. On `Right`, the response's own `data.displayName` (not the caller's input string
  verbatim) is what gets written to `AccountProfileLocalCache` and returned — defensive against the backend
  ever normalizing the value (e.g. trimming), so the cache can never drift from what the server actually
  confirmed.
- `clearCachedDisplayName()` — deletes the one Keychain key; called by both the logout and account-deletion
  flows (research.md R9).

## Scenario table (RNF09 — `account-settings-update` is a write endpoint; this unit extends its existing
coverage, RF03 having already covered the `biometricEnabled`-only body shape)

| # | Scenario | Expected `Either` | Local cache after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 200, `displayName` 1–80 chars | `Right(name)` | Written |
| 2 | Dio timeout | `Left(NetworkTimeoutFailure)` | Unchanged |
| 3 | No connection | `Left(NetworkOfflineFailure)` | Unchanged |
| 4 | 200 with a malformed body (`displayName` missing from the response) | `Left(ValidationFailure)` | Unchanged |
| 5 | 401 `AUTH_EXPIRED`, silent refresh succeeds | retried call's own result | per retried outcome |
| 6 | 401 `AUTH_EXPIRED`, silent refresh fails | `Left(AuthExpiredFailure)`, `reauthRequired` fires | Unchanged |

`SettingsBloc`'s own handling (not this repository's job) keeps `nameDraft`/edit mode intact on any `Left`
(FR-012) and returns the field to `viewing` mode showing the confirmed name only on a `Right`.

1	# Contract: `SettingsBloc`
2	
3	`features/settings/presentation/bloc/`. A `get_it` `registerFactory` (screen-scoped, same lifetime pattern as
4	`RecordsBloc`/`ExportBloc` — a fresh instance per `AppRoutes.settings` visit, never a singleton, since
5	FR-008/FR-023 require a fresh fetch on every open rather than a resumed prior state).
6	
7	## Dependencies
8	
9	`DashboardRepository`, `AccountProfileRepository`, `AccountDeletionRepository`, `AuthRepository`,
10	`SessionRepository`, `SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase`, `VaultRepository` — no `SessionBloc` import
11	(research.md R11 keeps that cross-bloc touch at the page, not the bloc, same as `RecordsBloc`).
12	
13	## Events
14	
15	| Event | Triggers |
16	|---|---|
17	| `SettingsOpened` | Dispatched once by the route builder (`app_router.dart`), mirroring `RecordsStarted`. Kicks off: aggregate fetch → (conditionally) narrative fetch; profile load (`SessionRepository`'s cached `Account.email` + `AccountProfileRepository.readCachedDisplayName()` or the email-derived default); biometric capability + current value. |
18	| `DashboardRetryRequested` | Re-runs the aggregate (and, if it then qualifies, narrative) fetch — FR-007's retry affordance. |
19	| `NameEditStarted` | `nameEditStatus → editing`, `nameDraft` seeded with the current `displayName`. |
20	| `NameDraftChanged(String value)` | Updates `nameDraft` only — no validation yet. |
21	| `NameEditCancelled` | `nameEditStatus → viewing`, `nameDraft` discarded. |
22	| `NameEditSubmitted` | Validates `nameDraft` first (FR-011); on failure, sets `nameEditFailureMessage`, stays `editing`, **no repository call**. On pass, calls `AccountProfileRepository.updateDisplayName`; on `Right`, `displayName` updates and `nameEditStatus → viewing`; on `Left`, stays `editing` with `nameDraft` intact and a retryable message (FR-012). |
23	| `BiometricToggleChanged(bool value)` | Optimistically flips `biometricEnabled` (RNF01), calls `SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase`; reverts + message on `Left` (contracts/biometric-preference-settings-extension.md). |
24	| `SignOutRequested` | contracts/account-session-actions.md. |
25	| `DeleteAccountDialogOpened` / `DeleteAccountDialogCancelled` | Presentation-only — toggles `deleteDialogOpen`; cancel makes **no** backend call (FR-021). |
26	| `DeleteAccountConfirmed` | contracts/account-deletion-repository.md. |
27	
28	## `reauthRequired` (research.md R11)
29	
30	```dart
31	final _reauthController = StreamController<void>.broadcast();
32	Stream<void> get reauthRequired => _reauthController.stream;
33	```
34	Fired from inside any repository-call handler whenever the result is `Left(AuthExpiredFailure)` *after* that
35	repository's own single silent-refresh retry has already been exhausted (never for the first attempt, which
36	retries silently without surfacing anything) — same trigger condition `RecordsBloc`/`ChatSessionsBloc` already
37	use for their own `reauthRequired` streams. `close()` overridden to also close `_reauthController`, mirroring
38	`RecordsBloc`.
39	
40	## `SettingsPage` wiring (`features/settings/presentation/pages/settings_page.dart`)
41	
42	```dart
43	late final StreamSubscription<void> _reauthSubscription;
44	
45	@override
46	void initState() {
47	  super.initState();
48	  _reauthSubscription = context.read<SettingsBloc>().reauthRequired.listen((_) {
49	    if (!mounted) return;
50	    context.read<SessionBloc>().add(const AuthExpiredDetected());
51	  });
52	}
53	```
54	A `BlocListener<SettingsBloc, SettingsState>` with `listenWhen` on `signedOutDestination`/
55	`accountDeletedDestination` becoming non-null performs the `context.go()` (research.md R10); a second
56	`BlocListener` (or the same one) shows the delete-confirmation `AlertDialog` while `deleteDialogOpen == true`,
57	closing it automatically on a successful deletion (the destination-change listener fires in the same frame).
58	
59	## Session-expiry mid-screen (spec.md Edge Cases; research.md R15)
60	
61	The existing `main.dart`-level `BlocListener<SessionBloc>` raises the overlay exactly as it does for every
62	other screen — no change there. Re-authenticating does **not** rebuild `SettingsPage`/`SettingsBloc` (the
63	reauth `LoginSignupPage` is pushed on top of, then popped back to, the same still-mounted `SettingsPage` —
64	`showSessionExpiredOverlay`'s own existing mechanism); instead, `SettingsPage`'s `State` is `RouteAware`,
65	subscribed to the already-existing `chatRouteObserver` (`app_router.dart`):
66	
67	```dart
68	@override
69	void didChangeDependencies() {
70	  super.didChangeDependencies();
71	  chatRouteObserver.subscribe(this, ModalRoute.of(context)! as PageRoute<void>);
72	}
73	
74	@override
75	void dispose() {
76	  chatRouteObserver.unsubscribe(this);
77	  super.dispose();
78	}
79	
80	@override
81	void didPopNext() => context.read<SettingsBloc>().add(const SettingsOpened());
82	```
83	
84	So the dashboard, profile, and biometric toggle are "reasonably re-requested" the moment the reauth page above
85	Settings is popped — matching spec.md's own wording, which is deliberately stronger here than Records'/Chat's
86	"preserve state, don't necessarily refetch" handling of the same overlay. An in-progress name edit
87	(`nameEditStatus == editing`, `nameDraft` holding unsaved text) is **not** reset by this `SettingsOpened`
88	re-dispatch — the handler only refills `dashboardStatus`/`aggregate`/`narrativeStatus`/`biometricEnabled`/
89	`displayName` (the latter only when not currently being edited), leaving `nameEditStatus`/`nameDraft` alone so
90	the user's in-progress text survives re-authentication too ("any in-progress edit... not silently lost").

1	# Contract: Settings' biometric toggle (research.md R6) — a new caller, zero changes to `vault/`
2	
3	`SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase` (`features/settings/domain/usecases/`):
4	
5	```dart
6	class SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase {
7	  const SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase({
8	    required BiometricsPreferenceRepository biometricsPreferenceRepository, // vault/domain/, unmodified
9	    required VaultRepository vaultRepository,                               // vault/domain/, unmodified
10	  });
11	
12	  Future<Either<Failure, void>> call(bool enabled) async {
13	    final result = await _biometricsPreferenceRepository.save(enabled);
14	    return result.match(
15	      (failure) => Left(failure), // local mirror left untouched — next relock still gates on the old value
16	      (_) async {
17	        await _vaultRepository.setBiometricPreferenceLocally(enabled);
18	        return const Right(null);
19	      },
20	    );
21	  }
22	}
23	```
24	
25	## Reads for the toggle's initial state / visibility (`SettingsBloc`, on `SettingsOpened`)
26	
27	```dart
28	final capability = await vaultRepository.checkBiometricCapability();
29	final visible = capability == BiometricCapability.available;         // FR-013's "hidden entirely" rule
30	final enabled = visible ? await vaultRepository.isBiometricPreferenceEnabled() : false;
31	```
32	`noHardware`/`notEnrolled`/`osDisabled` all resolve to `visible = false` — the same "all non-`available`
33	outcomes are routed identically" reading `VaultBloc`'s own `BiometricAuthOutcome` handling already
34	establishes for its own enum (RF03, contracts/vault-repository.md).
35	
36	## Scenario table
37	
38	| # | Scenario | `SettingsBloc` reaction |
39	|---|---|---|
40	| 1 | `checkBiometricCapability() == available` | Toggle row shown, initial value from `isBiometricPreferenceEnabled()` |
41	| 2 | `noHardware` / `notEnrolled` / `osDisabled` | Toggle row omitted entirely from `SettingsState` (`biometricToggleVisible = false`) — no disabled/grayed row |
42	| 3 | User flips the toggle; `save()` → `Right` | UI already shows the flipped value optimistically (RNF01, <100ms); `VaultRepository`'s mirror updated to match — confirmed |
43	| 4 | User flips the toggle; `save()` → `Left` (timeout/offline/malformed) | UI reverts to the pre-flip value, `biometricFailureMessage` set, mirror left untouched (FR-014) |
44	| 5 | `save()` returns `Left(AuthExpiredFailure)` after a failed silent refresh | Same revert as #4, plus `reauthRequired` fires |
45	
46	This usecase is exercised with `mocktail` fakes of `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`/`VaultRepository` — no new
47	test doubles for `local_auth`/`flutter_secure_storage` are needed, since neither is touched directly here.

2	
3	Phase 1 output. Field names are this unit's own typed wrapper around `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`'s
4	`/dashboard/*`/`/account*`/`/auth/logout` schemas (research.md R1/R6/R7/R8/R9) — where this document and the
5	contract ever disagree, the contract prevails (Constitution Principle I).
6	
7	## Domain entities (`lib/features/settings/domain/entities/`)
8	
9	### `AggregateBucket`
10	| Field | Type | Notes |
11	|---|---|---|
12	| `date` | `DateTime` | Parsed from the backend's `YYYY-MM-DD` string, date-only (no time component kept). |
13	| `count` | `int` | ≥ 0. |
14	| `sources` | `DashboardSourceCounts` | `{manual, audio, photo, chat}`, each `int` ≥ 0 — carried for completeness; this unit's chart only ever renders `count` (no per-source stacking/legend in scope). |
15	
16	### `DashboardTotals`
17	`{count: int, sources: DashboardSourceCounts}` — the account-wide total for the requested period.
18	
19	### `DashboardAggregate`
20	`{buckets: List<AggregateBucket>, totals: DashboardTotals}`. One pure extension method:
21	- `List<int> tenBars({DateTime? today})` → `research.md R2`'s `tenBars` function, `today` defaulting to
22	  `DateTime.now()` but overridable for deterministic tests.
23	
24	### `DashboardNarrative`
25	`{text: String, generatedAt: DateTime}` — `generatedAt` is parsed but never displayed (spec.md: the
26	narrative's own content/quality is out of scope); kept only because the response always carries it and
27	dropping a required field silently would be a worse modeling choice than keeping it unused.
28	
29	### `AccountProfile`
30	| Field | Type | Notes |
31	|---|---|---|
32	| `displayName` | `String` | 1–80 chars once set; the screen's single source of truth for both the name field and avatar initials. |
33	| `email` | `String` | Read-only in this unit (FR-009); sourced from `SessionRepository`'s already-resolved `Account.email`, never from a Settings-owned call. |
34	
35	Static/instance helpers (research.md R13):
36	- `static String defaultDisplayNameFromEmail(String email)` — splits the email's local part on `._-`,
37	  title-cases each word, joins with a space (`"wagner.duarte@x.com"` → `"Wagner Duarte"`); `email` itself if
